newsitem.title: USA: NYPA 832 MW Fitzpatrick nuke resumes power output.
newsitem.headline: NYPA 832 MW Fitzpatrick nuke resumes power output.

text.p: The New York Power Authority (NYPA) said its 832 megawatt Fitzpatrick nuclear power plant in Scriba N.Y., resumed electricity production Wednesday morning following a maintenance shutdown.
The unit was producing at 28 percent of capacity and had synchronized to the electricity grid as of Wednesday morning, spokesman Tim Carroll said.
The unit was expected to reach full power output within 24 hours, the spokesman said.
Fitzpatrick was shut on Thursday to clean away fish and debris which had accumulated on the screens in the plant's water intake system.
Water from the intakes cools the plant's condenser and is returned to Lake Ontario, NYPA said in a statement. The condenser cools steam which has been used to power the plant's turbine.
NYPA produces about 25 percent of New York state's power.
